content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., sentiment < 0.0) — model ignores bearish signals.  
- Overreact to short-term sentiment swings; model lags in adjusting to sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns sharply negative.  
- Mean-reversion bias: model holds prices too high in strong bullish sentiment and too low in strong bearish sentiment — fails to respect historical volatility clustering.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile — model is overly optimistic.  
- When sentiment is positive but recent prices are falling, model fails to anticipate reversal — underestimates downward correction.
